provenance.instrument: Code of the Township of Lower Makefield, Chapter 200 Zoning, as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 (code LO1561): includes legislation through 12-17-2025. New Laws (21). Two amend Chapter 200: Ord. No. 474 (2026-08-19, conditional uses in C-2) and Ord. No. 476 (2026-09-16, definition of 'structure'). Neither adds ADUs. Read in the eCode360 print view in a browser.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: Includes legislation through 12-17-2025. New Laws (21), two for Chapter 200 (Ord. 474 and 476), neither about dwellings.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, accessory apartment or in-law rule. Each residential district lists its uses 'and no other' (200-15, 200-20, 200-24, 200-28, 200-32)
R-1 and R-2 allow only single-family detached dwellings. A second unit on such a lot needs a use variance
A dwelling unit is a unit with living, sleeping, cooking, bathing and eating facilities for one family (200-7)

Two-family dwellings are a use by right in R-3 and R-4 (200-24A(4), 200-32A(5)). In R-3 they are a development type: 10-acre tract, 6,000 sq ft of net lot area per dwelling unit, 40% of the site in resource protection and open space (200-26A)

Boarding: up to two boarders in a single-family detached house by special exception in R-1, on 16,000 sq ft, with no added rooms. 'No separate cooking facilities or dwelling may be created' (200-15B(10), 200-69A(3)(b), (d))
Residential accessory buildings: behind the middle of the house depth, 15 ft high. 5 ft from side and rear lines under 200 sq ft, 10 ft from any line above 200 sq ft (200-69A(14)(a))
Parking: two spaces per dwelling unit for a single-family detached dwelling, 2.5 per unit for other residential uses (200-79A)

Short-term lodging is barred except owner-occupied rental of up to two bedrooms, or rental of a whole unit for 7 to 30 days. Each facility needs an annual license and may not be rented more than 120 days a year (130-3, 130-4)

Yards depend on the lot's size tier. R-1 (200-18): 1 acre and 40,000 sq ft lots 50/25/75 ft, 34,000 50/25/70, 25,000 and 22,000 40/20/70, 16,500 and 15,000 35/15/45. R-2 (200-22): 34,000 40/15/50, 16,000 and 15,000 35/15/45, 12,500 (cluster) 30/15/45. The district rows hold the smallest conventional tier
R-2 lots recorded before January 1, 1947 and 100 ft wide or less: two side yards of at least 10 ft each and 26 ft combined (200-22 note 3)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Community Development Department, https://www.lmt.org/departments/community-development/. Searched Chapter 200 for: accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, in-law, granny, elder cottage, ECHO, carriage, guest house, servant, caretaker, secondary dwelling, accessory living, second dwelling, accessory residential, living quarters, conversion, family suite. Pending: none for dwellings on the New Laws list. Review fixes 2026-11-11: R-2 minimum lot 15,000, lot tiers, boarding (d), short-term lodging license and 120 days.

term.note: No ADU term. Searched for accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, in-law, granny, elder cottage, ECHO, carriage, guest house, servant, caretaker, second dwelling, conversion.

status.note: The code has no ADU text.

path.note: R-1 lists uses 'and no other'. A second unit is not listed, so a use variance is the path. The code has no unlisted-use special exception.

fallback_path.note: A lot that fails a district rule also needs a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family dwelling (development)
value.conditions: Two-family dwellings as a development: minimum tract 10 acres, 6,000 sq ft of net lot area per dwelling unit, 4.5 units per acre, 40% of the site in resource protection and open space. Not a lot-by-lot option for an existing house.

value.name: Two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Use by right. Lot and tract standards of 200-34 not recorded here.

alternatives.note: No conversion of an existing house is listed.

historic_bypass.note: No ADU text, so no historic path.

value.condition: Short-term lodging is barred except owner-occupied rental of up to two bedrooms, or a whole unit for 7 to 30 days. Annual license. At most 120 days a year.
Residential accessory buildings stand only in side or rear yards 'behind the median line of the residential dwelling'.

gates.note: Rules that reach any second unit.

max_height_ft.note: Accessory rule, not an ADU rule: 'No accessory building or structure shall exceed 15 feet in height.'

setback_front_ft.note: No number. Not in front yards, and behind the median line of the house.

setback_side_ft.note: Buildings over 200 sq ft 'not less than 10 feet from any property line'. 5 ft under 200 sq ft.

setback_rear_ft.note: Same as side. 5 ft under 200 sq ft.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: Detached accessory buildings use the 5 and 10 ft rules. A garage joined by a breezeway is part of the principal building and meets district yards.

internal_uses_district_height.note: A unit inside or attached to the house takes the 35 ft district height.

family_only.note: No ADU rule. A family is related persons or up to five unrelated persons, excluding servants, with single cooking facilities.

short_term_rental_banned.note: No ADU rule. Short-term lodging is limited town-wide: two bedrooms in an owner-occupied house, or a whole unit for 7 to 30 days, with an annual license and at most 120 days a year.

max_adus.note: Reading: 0 means the code allows no ADU.

reading.value: No ADU row. Single-family detached: two spaces per dwelling unit. If the second unit counts as a dwelling unit, four. Other residential uses need 2.5 per unit.

min_lot_sqft.note: Lot size depends on resource protection land: 34,000 sq ft (0% to 24%), 22,000 (25% to 67%), 15,000 (68% and up) (200-16B). 34,000 with on-lot water or sewer. Yards depend on the lot tier (200-18). This row holds the 15,000 sq ft tier.

setback_front_ft.note: Depends on lot tier. Front 35 ft for 15,000 and 16,500 sq ft lots. 40 ft for 22,000 and 25,000. 50 ft for 34,000 sq ft and up.

setback_side_ft.note: Depends on lot tier. Side 15 ft each for 15,000 and 16,500 sq ft lots. 20 ft for 22,000 and 25,000. 25 ft for 34,000 sq ft and up.

setback_rear_ft.note: Depends on lot tier. Rear 45 ft for 15,000 and 16,500 sq ft lots. 70 ft for 22,000 to 34,000. 75 ft for 40,000 sq ft and 1 acre.

yard_tiers.note: Rows by 'Minimum Net Lot Area'. Reading: a lot takes the row of the largest tier it meets. A yard on a collector or arterial road is 80 or 100 ft (note 1).

min_lot_sqft.note: Conventional single-family lot: 34,000 sq ft (0% to 24% resource protection land), 16,000 (25% to 45%), 15,000 (46% and up). Open space cluster lots: 10,000 minimum and 12,500 average, only where resource protection land exceeds 51% (200-22.1).

setback_front_ft.note: Depends on lot tier. 35 ft for 15,000 and 16,000 sq ft lots. 40 ft for 34,000 and 16,500. 30 ft for the 12,500 sq ft cluster row.

setback_side_ft.note: 15 ft each in every tier. Lots recorded before 1947 and 100 ft wide or less: 10 ft each, 26 ft combined.

setback_rear_ft.note: Depends on lot tier. 45 ft for lots of 16,000 sq ft and under. 50 ft for 34,000 and 16,500.

value.note: 12,500 sq ft row, open space cluster lots only.

yard_tiers.note: Rows by 'Minimum Net Lot Area'. Reading: a lot takes the row of the largest tier it meets. Lots recorded before 1947 and 100 ft wide or less: side yards 10 ft each, 26 ft combined (note 3).
